svg.text: Q8 Strip reference circuits, redrawn from Quad Eight MM-310 BL (drawing 3891) and AM-4B (drawing 30024-03)
Values were read from scanned drawings. Check them against your originals before building. Red text = what the plugin does with that part.
A. EQ amplifier A2 (MM-310 BL). Flat gain = 0.5 x (1 + R14/R11) = 1.7. Band networks (Part B) attach at nets N+ and N-
DSP: EQ output is gain-normalised to unity,
so flat = 0 dB (real stage is +4.6 dB)
B. One EQ band (LF shown). A resonant series L-C branch; the stepped 2k control sets the resistance in series with it
(ladder R58-R61, R33 on one side; R53-R56, R30 on the other)
BOOST: branch sits on N- (inverting leg). Gain = 1 + k s C / D(s), k = R14 / (1 + R14/R11) = 7.06k
CUT: branch sits on N+ (non-inverting leg). Gain = D(s) / (D(s) + 5k s C), 5k = R12 || R13
D(s) = L C s^2 + R C s + 1. R = control resistance + inductor loss. Lower R = deeper and narrower.
Peak gain at resonance: boost = 1 + 7.06k / R, cut = R / (R + 5k). The plugin solves R for the gain knob value.
Inductor loss (Q of 12 / 15 / 15 for LF / MF / HF) is my assumption, not read from the schematic.
C. Band frequencies and tuning capacitors read from the MM-310 BL. L is derived: L = 1 / ((2 pi f)^2 C)
Caps are in microfarads. The tapped inductors are L1/L2 (LF), L3 (MF), L4 (HF). S6B and C38-C41 (.047 / .02 / .025 / .02 uF) look like an alternate HF network; the plugin does not model it.
D. AM-4B discrete op-amp (the gain block inside the module). Class-A differential pair, PNP voltage stage, complementary follower output
DSP: the pair + PNP stage + complementary
follower is the asymmetric tanh preamp stage
(part numbers as read from the scan)
E. Whole strip, in the same order as the plugin chain

Notes: (1) The preamp stage and EQ order follow the MM-310 BL (mic/line amp, then EQ amp A2, then fader and line amp A3). The high-pass and compressor are utility stages I added; the schematics you sent do not show them.

(2) In your upload, the first image is the EQ-312E sheet (same LC band approach, plus a +/-15 dB trim ladder R200-R206). Images 2 and 3 are the two halves of the MM-310 BL. The lower right of image 4 is a Sphere Electronics mic amp, not Quad Eight.
(3) Safety: build and test the line-level stages on a bench supply first. Do not wire mains or 48 V phantom circuits without a proper supply design.
